problem: Which of the following gives the equation of the tangent to the curve $r(t)=({t}^{2}-1)\,i+\sqrt{1+{t}^{2}}\,j+(t-1)\,k$ at the point corresponding to $t=2,$  valid for all  real values of $u?$

activity_context.topic_title: Tangent Vectors and Tangent Lines to Curves

examples.knowledge_point: Finding a Tangent Line to a Curve
examples.problem: Find a parametrization of the tangent line to the curve $\mathbf r(t)=\left\langle \cos{t}, \: \sin{t},\: 4t^2\right\rangle$ at the point where $t=\dfrac{\pi}{2}.$
examples.worked_solution:
Let  $P$ be the point at the tip of the vector $\mathbf r\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right ).$  At this point,  the vector $\mathbf r'\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right )$ is tangent to the curve, so the tangent line to the curve at $P$ can be parametrized as

$$
\mathbf R(u)=\mathbf r\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right )+u \, \mathbf r'\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right ), \qquad u \in (-\infty, \infty).
$$

 

First, we find $\mathbf r\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) \mathbin{:}$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}r(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,4{(\frac{\pi }{2})}^{2}⟩=⟨0,1,{\pi }^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now,  we calculate $\mathbf r'(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=\dfrac{\pi}{2}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,8t⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,8(\frac{\pi }{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,0,4\pi ⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the tangent line to the given curve at the point $P$ where $t=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(u)=⟨0,1,{\pi }^{2}⟩+u⟨-1,0,4\pi ⟩,\,u\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: Find a tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=(3t+2)\,i+(6t+1)\,j+(1-4{t}^{2})\,k$ at the point $P(2,1,1).$
feedback.worked_solution:
The point $P(2,1,1)$ is at the tip of $r(t)$ for some specific value ${t}_{0}$ of the parameter $t.$ At this point, the vector ${r}^{′}({t}_{0})$ is tangent to the curve.

First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to $P.$ We know that

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =2\,i+j+k \\ (3t+2)\,i+(6t+1)\,j+(1-4{t}^{2})\,k & =2\,i+j+k,\end{aligned}
$$

and equating the coefficients of $i,j,$ and $k$ yields the following system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}3t+2=2 \\ 6t+1=1 \\ 1-4{t}^{2}=1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equation, we get $t=0.$ This value also satisfies the other two equations. Therefore, $P(2,1,1)$ is at the tip of the vector $r(0).$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3t+2)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6t+1)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-4{t}^{2})\,k \\  & =3\,i+6\,j-8t\,k \\ {r}^{′}(0) & =3\,i+6\,j-8(0)\,k \\  & =3\,i+6\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a tangent vector to the given curve at the point $P(2,1,1)$ is $3\,i+6\,j.$
